fundamental_comparison: metabolic_relaxation is more fundamental: one local signed energy-difference update drives retention and release, while metabolic_gate adds separate energy-to-speed, retention, and exploration heuristics; gate's speed term is directly hard-coded motor control.
novelty_comparison: neither is novel at the mechanism level: signed outcome plasticity overlaps dopamine/RPE and LTP/LTD (PMC8066851), while energy/activity stabilization overlaps homeostatic synaptic plasticity (PMC3249629). relaxation is marginally closer to one reusable law; no novelty claim is justified without signed-vs-positive and certainty/evidence ablations.
scaling_comparison: metabolic_gate has the better engineering scaling prospect (constant three-channel state and O(batch) operations) and the stronger measured score, but it does not grow or prune and hard-codes three colors. relaxation is also constant-state, yet structure() reports connections=batch*3, so its scaling claim is currently not a valid brain-size measure.
caveat: The no-interoception run exposes an input-contract bug in both candidates: with 48 sensors they still treat sensors[:,-1] as energy and infer 15 pixels, so this is not a clean ablation.

fundamental_comparison: axiom has the stronger single-law story because signed metabolic consequence can encode approach and avoidance in one local trace update; gate is three separate energy heuristics (retention, memory gain, exploration) and fixed motor speed. However the current leaderboard does not attribute the gain to signed credit: both candidates score exactly 2.8408203125, while the reported 2.4023 ablation is a different metabolic_gate implementation. In the controlled audit, gate trace after gain/loss was [0.6,0,0] then [0,0,0], whereas axiom was [0.6,0,0] then [-0.07946,0,0]. Both still hard-code three color channels and Braitenberg eye-to-turn plus bite threshold.
novelty_comparison: Neither mechanism is established as novel. Gate overlaps homeostatic synaptic scaling/activity stabilization (PMC3249629) and reward-gated plasticity; axiom's signed outcome delta overlaps dopamine prediction-error learning (PMC7804370) and interoceptive prediction-error/active-inference models (PMC4731102). Axiom is marginally more distinctive only as reward-free interoceptive signed credit, but this needs same-seed signed-vs-positive, loss-gate, and speed ablations before a novelty claim.
scaling_comparison: Gate has a slight engineering advantage: fixed speed, fewer parameters, and O(batch*3) state/updates. Axiom has the same asymptotic cost but adds loss and energy-speed heuristics. Neither scales as a brain: structure() remains units=3, connections=3 at steps 0 and 6000 for n_units=302, and both ignore n_units/growth/pruning. The no-intero contract is also invalid in both: with 48 sensors each reads sensors[:,-1] as phantom energy and infers 15 pixels.

evidence_update: odkrywca_life reports fixed-speed ablation score 2.8408203125 > metabolic_gate 2.40234375 and ungated_trace 2.03125; this supports energy gating of sensory trace while energy-speed coupling is harmful. It does not isolate signed credit because no same-seed signed-vs-positive comparison against axiom is supplied.
code_audit: axiom_signed_ema uses signed delta with fixed EMA leak and constant speed 0.575; it removes axiom's loss gate and energy-speed mapping, but retains the same three-color outcome trace and hard-coded eye-to-turn/bite policy. Its score is below metabolic_gate_fixed_speed (2.8408203125); this is not evidence signed trace helps. The organism-v4 protocol is not directly comparable to the v3 leader without a same-protocol rerun. Structure still does not grow or prune.
prior_art: Opened sources PMC7804370 dopamine prediction errors; PMC4731102 interoceptive prediction errors/active inference; PMC3249629 homeostatic plasticity. Mechanism-level novelty remains unestablished.
